helpful: The provisioned snapshot carried the full docket through the merits calendar (grant, argument date, petitioners' merits brief), so no MCP docket retrieval was needed.
The statpack merits section's per-Term disturbed table with the excluded-count guard made the pooled baseline a five-minute computation with clear quotability rules.
gaps: No free-text/semantic corpus search: `fedcourts query` is structured-filter only, so there is no way to pull doctrinally similar priors (e.g. federal-common-law borrowing cases) for a merits cell.
The citation filter's coverage is very thin (161 of ~590k SCOTUS rows), so known-case lookups mostly return empty.

No PDF text extraction for docket-linked filings beyond the provisioned cert documents: the SG's CVSG brief and the merits briefs are on the docket as URLs, but I had to rely on secondary press summaries for the SG's position. A document-fetch tool that extracts text from supremecourt.gov PDFs would have materially improved this forecast.
notes: Forward merits cell at moment: grant. The decisive signal (SG's CVSG position) came from web search summaries rather than a primary source; see reasoning.md for the discount.
